speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE) with secondary intraventricular hemorrhage. The clinical picture of a 31-week preterm infant with severe chorioamnionitis, Apgar scores of 3 and 6, history of hypoxia, lethargy, poor tone, irregular respirations, and a tense anterior fontanelle strongly points to brain injury from perinatal asphyxia. The specific finding of a tense fontanelle raises concern for intraventricular hemorrhage, which is common in this gestational age. We must rule out sepsis and metabolic causes, but HIE is the primary working diagnosis.
